subject: LyraPay security qualification — recap & agreed next steps
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Emilia Torres <emilia.t@lyrapay.com>, procurement@lyrapay.com
Cc: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 14:12:00 -0800
Subject: LyraPay security qualification — recap & agreed next steps

Hi Emilia — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap of what we heard and the concrete next steps so everyone is aligned. Please flag anything I missed.

Summary of LyraPay priorities / pain points
- Long-term audit log retention requirement: 6–7 years for transaction traces (legal/procurement requirement).
- SOC 2 Type II evidence required for hosted vendors + a request for the pen-test window and remediation cadence.
- DPA needs explicit language on access controls, KMS integration, and deletion/retention clauses.
- Prefer logs with identifiable fields (request_id, customer_id, timestamp, action) — procurement will validate this.

What Redwood committed to (high level)
- Provide our SOC 2 Type II report summary and a redacted artifact list (attached stub).
- Deliver an audit_log_sample.csv (anonymized) showing fields and retention lifecycle.
- Share a DPA draft with our suggested retention wording + KMS notes; we’ll accept reasonable redlines but will need legal to review.
- Clarify pen-test cadence and our remediation SLA (we run annual third-party pen tests and push critical fixes with a 30-day target).

Agreed next steps (owners & dates)
1) Redwood: Send SOC 2 summary + artifact index (jonas) — by 2026-11-18 EOD. Attachment: SOC2_Type2_summary_stub.pdf
2) Redwood: Share anonymized audit log sample (irene) — by 2026-11-18 EOD. Attachment: audit_log_sample_2026-11.csv
3) LyraPay: Confirm fields required for logs and any retention overflow ask (Emilia / procurement) — by 2026-11-20.
4) Redwood legal & LyraPay legal to start DPA redline (marissa to share initial DPA_draft.docx) — redline in 1 week.
5) Schedule follow-up technical sync to validate log shape + retention policy (30-minute call) — propose Wed, 2026-11-24. I included a calendar poll link below.

If this aligns, I’ll drop these attachments now and send a calendar invite for Wed 11/24 (or we can move earlier if you need a faster turn).

Calendar poll: https://calendly.com/jonas-weber/lyrapay-security-sync

Thanks — Jonas
Jonas Weber
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0136

Thanks Jonas — that matches our notes from the call. A couple of clarifications from procurement/ops:

- Retention: our legal team requires evidence that transaction-level logs can be retained for up to 7 years and exported on request. If your hosted default is shorter, we need to understand the upgrade path and any incremental costs.
- Pen test: can you confirm whether pen tests include both hosted control plane and the inference runtime (GPU instances)? We need scope details to satisfy our security team.
- DPA: we’ll circulate initial redlines focused on retention & deletion language; procurement copied here (procurement@lyrapay.com).

I’m attaching a short vendor evidence checklist that our security team uses — helps speed reviews.

We can do the technical sync on 11/24 AM PST. If Redwood needs to propose a different slot, let us know.

Best,
Emilia

emilia.t@lyrapay.com

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Emilia Torres <emilia.t@lyrapay.com>
Date: Tue, 17 Nov 2026 09:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: LyraPay security qualification — recap & agreed next steps

Adding a few technical clarifications and internal action updates.

Quick tech notes:
- Audit logs: default hosted retention is 13 months in the standard offering. Long-term retention (multi-year) is supported via our cold-archive export pipeline; we can store for 7 years but that is a delegated archive feature that requires a dedicated retention addendum (typical for enterprise customers). There will be a storage-based incremental charge; I’ll surface ballpark numbers after scope confirmation.
- Log fields: our sample will include request_id, user_id (hashed), customer_id (hashed), timestamp (UTC), model_id, tokens_generated, action_type. If LyraPay needs PII in logs, we’ll need to discuss masking rules and legal constraints.
- Pen test scope: our most recent third-party pen test included both control plane and runtime network configurations (we can share scope statement). Runtime host-level access is restricted; inference containers do not expose host SSH.

Deliverables I’ll provide by 2026-11-18 EOD:
- audit_log_sample_2026-11.csv (anonymized)
- pen_test_scope_statement.pdf (extract)
- short note on archive export process and estimated storage delta (1–2 paragraphs)

Internal ask for Marissa: please prepare the DPA draft with retention clause language we typically offer for enterprise archive (I can get a sample clause if that helps).

Irene
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
irene.choi@redwood.com

Appreciate the fast turnaround, Irene — and thanks Emilia for the checklist. Confirming next steps and timeline:

- Today (11/18 EOD): SOC2 summary + audit log sample + pen test scope extract (sent).
- 11/20: LyraPay to confirm any additional required log fields and the retention acceptance criteria.
- 11/24: Technical sync (30 min) to validate sample and discuss retention pricing. I’ll send two calendar invites (AM and late-PST) so you can pick.
- Legal: Marissa will send the initial DPA draft to your counsel; we ask for redlines within 7 business days to keep the commercial timeline moving.

If you need anything sooner, ping me directly. Looking forward to moving this to procurement and contracting — we should be able to present a scoped retention addendum and cost estimate within 5 business days after your field confirmation.

Thanks — Jonas
